batches.title: Hard-Boiled Eggs (Mon–Thu breakfasts)
steps: 1. Place 16 large eggs in a large pot in a single layer (2 eggs × 2 people × 4 days = 16 eggs).
2. Cover with cold water by at least 2 cm.
3. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
4. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium and cook exactly 10 minutes.
5. While eggs cook, prepare a large bowl of ice water.
6. Transfer eggs immediately to the ice bath using a slotted spoon. Leave 10 minutes until completely cold.
7. Peel all eggs gently under cold running water.
8. Pat dry with paper towel. Store in an airtight container in the fridge. Label: 'Boiled eggs — prepared Sunday, use by Thursday (day 4).'
9. Use 2 eggs per person each morning Monday through Thursday.
yields: 16 peeled hard-boiled eggs, stored in fridge up to 4 days

day_of_assembly.Monday: Breakfast — Kefir & Blueberry Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough: retrieve 2 eggs per person, halve onto toasted sourdough, drizzle olive oil.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Breakfast — Kefir & Strawberry Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough: retrieve 2 eggs per person, halve onto sourdough toast with olive oil drizzle.
day_of_assembly.Wednesday: Breakfast — Kefir & Blueberry Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough: retrieve 2 eggs per person (day 3 — safe), halve and arrange on toasted sourdough.
day_of_assembly.Thursday: Breakfast — Kefir & Banana Smoothie + Boiled Eggs on Sourdough: retrieve last 2 eggs per person (day 4 — within safe window), serve on toast with olive oil.

storage.safety_note: Hard-boiled eggs: 1 week in shell, 5 days peeled in water. Scrambled/cooked dishes: 3–4 days.

batches.title: Roasted Bell Peppers & Zucchini (Mon & Tue lunches)
steps: 1. Preheat oven to 210°C (fan 190°C).
2. Wash and deseed 3 large red bell peppers and 2 large yellow bell peppers. Cut into 3–4 cm strips.
3. Wash 2 medium zucchini; cut into 1 cm half-rounds.
4. Spread pepper strips on one large baking tray; spread zucchini on a second tray (or use two oven racks). Do not overcrowd.
5. Drizzle peppers with 1 tbsp olive oil; season with salt, black pepper, ½ tsp paprika. Toss well.
6. Drizzle zucchini with 1 tbsp olive oil; season with salt, ½ tsp dried oregano. Toss well.
7. Roast 22–25 minutes, turning once halfway, until edges are lightly charred and veg is tender.
8. Remove from oven; allow to cool completely (at least 20 min) before storing.
9. Transfer roasted peppers and zucchini to separate airtight containers. Label with today's date. Refrigerate. Safe up to 4 days (use by Thursday).
10. Portion for Monday lunch: 120 g mix (Diego), 90 g mix (Diana). Portion for Tuesday lunch: 100 g peppers (Diego), 80 g peppers (Diana).
yields: Approx 700 g roasted bell peppers + 400 g roasted zucchini, refrigerated

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl: microwave 120 g (Diego) / 90 g (Diana) roasted pepper-zucchini mix 60 sec; layer over quinoa with seared beef strips and lentils.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Lunch — Mexican Beef & Black Bean Bowl: microwave 100 g (Diego) / 80 g (Diana) roasted peppers 60 sec; spoon alongside browned ground beef, black beans and warm corn tortillas.

storage.safety_note: Cooked vegetables store well. Roasted veg can be eaten cold in salads.

batches.title: Cooked Quinoa (Mon lunch)
steps: 1. Rinse 200 g dry quinoa under cold water in a fine sieve for 1 minute to remove bitterness.
2. Place rinsed quinoa in a medium saucepan with 400 ml cold water and a pinch of salt.
3. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 12–14 minutes until water is absorbed and tails have unfurled.
4. Remove from heat; let stand covered 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
5. Spread on a plate to cool for 15 minutes — do not refrigerate warm to avoid moisture build-up.
6. Transfer to an airtight container. Label with date. Refrigerate. Safe up to 3 days (use Monday only from this batch — extra kept as backup).
yields: Approx 400 g cooked quinoa (from 200 g dry)

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl: scoop 120 g (Diego) / 80 g (Diana) cooked quinoa into bowl; microwave 90 sec; use as base for beef, lentils and roasted veg.

storage.safety_note: Add a splash of water before reheating to restore moisture. Use within 3 days.

batches.title: Boiled Waxy Potatoes (Wed lunch)
steps: 1. Scrub 800 g waxy potatoes (grenaille or Charlotte) well under cold water — leave skins on.
2. Place in a pot, cover with cold salted water by 3 cm.
3. Bring to a boil over high heat; cook 18–22 minutes until a knife inserts easily with no resistance.
4. Drain; allow to steam-dry in colander 5 minutes.
5. Cool to room temperature (do not refrigerate warm). Transfer to airtight container; refrigerate.
6. Label with Sunday's date. Safe in fridge up to 3 days — use Wednesday (day 3, within window).
7. Per serving: Diego uses 2 medium potatoes (approx 200 g); Diana uses 1.5 medium (approx 150 g).

day_of_assembly.Wednesday: Lunch — French-Style Salmon Niçoise Bowl: retrieve potatoes, halve them; arrange cold over mixed greens with chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber and freshly pan-cooked salmon; dress with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.

storage.safety_note: Cooked vegetables store well. Roasted veg can be eaten cold in salads.
